newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta says Timor bishop's explanation late.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta says Timor bishop's explanation late.

text.p: Jakarta said on Tuesday Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo had been slow in denying remarks ascribed to him likening Indonesian troops to "scabby dogs" and asked him to be careful in future.

"The Indonesian government can understand the explanation and apology of Bishop Belo," Susilo Sudarman, coordinating minister for politics and security affairs, was quoted by the official Antara news agency as saying.

But the government was concerned that last month's report in the German magazine Der Spiegel, in which Belo was quoted as saying Indonesian troops treated East Timorese like "scabby dogs" and "slaves", had been harmful to the nation's stability.

"The government regrets the long time it took to offer the explanation as it created nervousness in society," Sudarman was quoted as saying after a meeting of high-ranking officials including members of the cabinet and the armed forces chief.
"The government hopes that in the future Belo will be careful in his speech and actions so that they cannot be manipulated by irresponsible parties."

Belo told a news conference on Monday that his words had been "heavily manipulated and heavily distorted" by Der Spiegel. The correspondent who conducted the interview has said he stands by his story.
Thousands of youths linked to Indonesia's ruling Golkar party protested outside Jakarta's parliament last week and demanded a public apology from Belo, who was then in Jakarta.

The public criticism of Belo angered East Timorese and sparked protests in his defence by students in the provincial capital of Dili. More than 60,000 people gathered to welcome the bishop home on his return from the Indonesian capital.
Many East Timorese resent the rule of Indonesia, which annexed the former Portuguese colony in 1976 following an armed invasion the previous year.
The United Nations continues to reject Indonesian claims to sovereignty and considers Portugal the administering power.
